target_hash_note: the recheck report (verify/recheck.json) carries no target_hash field for a record target

overall.summary: Every stated number reproduces and the structure is sound; the centre-control reading holds at population level, but some supporting probes are outside the data support, the top rows go against the centre reading, and about a quarter of one override group does not need the thresholds.

findings.statement: structural and compositional coverage 1.0, hierarchy complete, one leaf and one composition, no splits or identity nodes
findings.evidence: recomputed 1.0 / 1.0, no uncovered nodes or edges, single root win_vote containing the output; op counts rename_node 42, annotate 2
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify recheck <record.json> --out verify/recheck.json

findings.statement: each unit = relu of a weighted sum of the standardised squares (coefficients rounded, approximate, off by up to 0.069, exit scale 26.1)
findings.check: own extraction of the genome's weights compared with the closed form
findings.evidence: unit 1: a1 0.0448, a2 0.424, a3 -1.24, bias 2.51; unit 2: a1 0.862 (all match to 3 s.f.); every input feeds all 32 units (1344 edges)

findings.statement: straightening one unit costs at most 0.020 of AUC (unit 5, the largest); all together 0.948 -> 0.854
findings.evidence: full 0.9482, all affine 0.8545; unit 5 alone drop 0.0204, the largest (next unit 23, 0.0165)
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify linearise <record.json> --level nodes

findings.statement: centre columns c-e: x ahead by 2+ 5546 positions, 92% (obs 92%); o ahead 5659, 35% (35%); column d: 2710, 98%; 2708, 30%; outer bottom row a1,b1,f1,g1: x ahead 7635, 42%; o ahead 6587, 88%
findings.check: own recomputation on the training split

findings.statement: six square-value bands: 7740 / 23%, 7662 / 42%, 10737 / 60%, 10890 / 78%, 8260 / 89%, 8756 / 97% (observed 23, 42, 59, 77, 90, 97%); weights are the standard lines-of-four table
findings.check: own square-value score (3-4-5-7 / 4-6-8-10 / 5-8-11-13 table) and bands

findings.statement: overrides: 111 positions scoring 6+ but predicted below one half, x wins 30% (mean prediction 32%); 1450 scoring below -6 predicted above one half, x wins 79% (77%); outcomes side with the model
findings.check: own recomputation; the same on the test split as a check
findings.evidence: train 111 / obs 0.297 / pred 0.320; 1450 / obs 0.795 / pred 0.772. Test split: 34 / obs 0.29 / pred 0.32; 357 / obs 0.75 / pred 0.77, so it is not a training-fit artefact

findings.statement: These overrides are the position-specific corrections that the thresholds add.
findings.check: replace every unit by its least-squares affine fit on its pre-activation and re-predict the two override groups
findings.evidence: group 1 (111): the straightened model puts all 111 above one half (mean 0.94), so these do come from the thresholds. Group 2 (1450): the straightened model still predicts above one half for 24% (352) of them (mean 0.30), so about a quarter of these overrides do not need the thresholds (own affine fit, all-affine AUC 0.847 vs the tool's 0.854, so the share is approximate)

findings.statement: the bottom-left corner a1 is a strong lever ... the a1 change carries it: changing d1 alone gives 68% (row 34); d1 alone giving 39% (row 15258)
findings.check: piece counts of the constructed boards; in-support swaps of every square with every opposite-colour piece over the training rows
findings.evidence: the swaps reproduce (row 34: 0.699 -> 0.015; 15258: 0.393 -> 0.927; 661: 0.738 -> 0.220; 1309: 0.799 -> 0.995) and keep 4 x and 4 o pieces. The 'one square alone' comparisons do not: flipping one piece gives 5-3 or 3-5 boards, and every training row has exactly 4 and 4, so 'd1 alone 68%' and 'the a1 change carries it' are extrapolation. In-support, a1 is the most negative commonly filled square (mean change -0.21 in predicted win when x takes it in a swap, 64,864 swaps), g1 -0.19, so the a1 reading is right in direction but its support is weaker than stated

findings.statement: No unit is a clean Connect-4 feature on its own; the thresholds work as a population
findings.check: each unit's correlation with the square-value score and its single-unit AUC
findings.evidence: the cited evidence (linearisation cost) speaks to non-linearity, not nameability; own check: no unit correlates above 0.42 with the score (unit 28), best single-unit AUC 0.656 (unit 1) against the model's 0.948, all-straightened drop 0.094

findings.statement: positive-weight units 1,3,4,6,7,9,10,15,16,19,21,24,26,28,32 off: mean change 0.65, AUC 0.948 -> 0.625; negative-weight units (2,5,8,...,31) off: -0.34, AUC 0.728; sigmoid of a weighted sum
findings.check: own output weights and ablation to zero
findings.evidence: the sign lists match the output weights exactly (15 positive, 17 negative); with-minus-without 0.650 and -0.337; AUC without 0.625 and 0.728; output activation sigmoid

findings.statement: In training row 34, turning o's a1 piece into an x piece lowers the predicted win from 70% to below 1%; unit 6 2.20 -> 0.00, 16 3.04 -> 0.17, 19 4.54 -> 2.32, 30 0.00 -> 1.25, 2 1.40 -> 3.58
findings.check: own forward pass of the constructed board; piece counts of the training rows
findings.evidence: all values reproduce (0.699 -> 0.005; unit values exactly as stated), and the case is labelled constructed, but it gives x five pieces and o three, a board that never occurs in training (all rows 4 and 4). That an extra x piece drops x's win to below 1% is the model extrapolating, so it illustrates the vote's mechanics but is not evidence about positions the model was trained on

findings.statement: x pieces in the centre columns raise it and x pieces on the outer bottom-row squares lower it (overall_function: 'much like the classic count of lines of four through each square')
findings.check: in-support swaps per square (x takes the square from o, o takes another square from x), mean change in predicted win over all training rows; linear fit of the logit on the 84 square indicators
findings.evidence: holds for rows 1-4 of the centre (d3 +0.51, c3 +0.38, e3 +0.30, d2 +0.30, d1 +0.26) and the corners a1 -0.21, g1 -0.19, but b1 -0.07 and f1 -0.02 are near neutral, and x pieces high in the centre columns lower the prediction (c6 -0.52, d6 -0.34, c5 -0.22, d5 -0.14), where the classic table gives d5 10 and d6 7. Overall the score explains 55% of the logit's variance (r 0.74; score alone AUC 0.820 vs model 0.948); per-square effects correlate 0.79 with the table

findings.statement: straightening any one unit costs at most 0.020; the d3/a1 swap in row 1309 raises 80% -> 99%; inputs fan out to more units than a split can copy (26-letter limit)
findings.check: linearise, own probe, code and weights
findings.evidence: 0.0204; 0.799 -> 0.995; each input feeds 32 units and explaneat/core/operations.py raises 'Too many splits, ran out of letters'

findings.statement: domain reading: centre control by the lines-of-four square-value heuristic, with position-specific corrections
findings.evidence: stated in Connect-4 terms (who controls the centre, square values, corners), not a restatement of the closed form; the 'partial' label the record gives is apt

board_detectors.why: The square-value centre-control reading is confirmed band by band (score explains 55% of the logit variance, per-square effects correlate 0.79 with the table), but it fails in the top rows and the thresholds' corrections (AUC 0.854 -> 0.948) are described only by effect, not by a rule.
